_comment: Describes the patch currently being built, and nothing else. Emptied
after each release — it says what is new in THIS version, not what the
Everything under backend/ and frontend/ (channel packs included) is
carried by every patch automatically and does not need naming here.
What goes here is the handful of things a patch has to ask the machine
to do rather than simply hand it:
notes             shown to the user when the update is offered
min_app_version   refuse to apply on anything older; use it when a
version depends on a change an earlier patch made
pip               libraries to install into the existing runtime
models            weights to fetch, by URL, once
fonts             a face to register with Windows as well as serve
rebuild_launcher  true only when updater/launcher.py itself changed
requires_setup    a sentence saying why a patch cannot do this one;
set it and the updater sends the user to the full
See installer/build_patch.py for the long version.
notes: Extracting frames from a video no longer fails with a screenful of file paths ending in a ten-digit number
When ffmpeg does fail, the window now shows what ffmpeg itself said went wrong - a corrupt download, an unreadable file - instead of the command that was run
ffmpeg is now run in its own window-less console, so an extraction can no longer be killed part-way by a Ctrl+C or a console closing elsewhere on the machine
That is what the failure on Undercover CEO was: ffmpeg was stopped from outside rather than failing on its own, and the app reported it as an extraction error
_comment_pip: The background-removal runtime. Ordinary install — measured against
this project's own pins it moves neither numpy nor opencv, so it needs
none of the --no-deps care simple-lama-inpainting does.
...and the speech recognition the Snapchat captions are read from.
Same story: an ordinary install that moves neither numpy nor opencv,
which is exactly why it is faster-whisper and not openai-whisper —
that one pulls numba, and numba moves numpy. See requirements.txt.
ctranslate2 is pinned under faster-whisper rather than left to it:
the version its own requirement resolves to crashes on load. See
requirements.txt for what was measured. The order matters — pip
would otherwise pull the broken one back over this pin.
All three are listed here as well as in requirements.txt because a
patch does not re-run Setup: an installed runtime only gains a
library if the patch asks for it by name.
_comment_models: The U2-Net weights the cutout is produced by. Fetched here rather than
carried, for the reason a patch is a megabyte at all: it is 176 MB of
file that never changes, and a machine that already has it skips this
It lands under backend/models/, which is named in
updater.KEEP_ACROSS_UPDATES — app/ is replaced wholesale by every
patch, and without that this would be re-downloaded by each one.
The app can also fetch it itself, at startup, if this never runs (see
background_remover.preload). Declared here anyway so it arrives with
the update rather than in front of the user's first cutout.
The Whisper weights the captions are read from are deliberately NOT
here. They are not one file but a directory, and they are named by
size rather than by URL — faster-whisper resolves them itself into
backend/models/whisper/, which is inside the same kept directory as
everything above. So they arrive the other way this list allows: the
app fetches them in its own startup warm-up (transcriber.preload),
once, on the first machine-lifetime that needs them. Until they land,
captured frames simply come back without captions.
